paper.title: A thousand empirical adaptive landscapes and their navigability
paper.supplied_bibliography_errors: The Nature publisher page confirms the title and the authors José Aguilar-Rodríguez, Joshua L. Payne, and Andreas Wagner; no discrepancy with the task citation was found.

sources.what: Reused existing author-hosted main article PDF; original download is in the prior core-literature dossier.
Reused existing Nature supplementary-information PDF; original download is in the prior core-literature dossier.

overlaps.locator: Results, ‘Landscape navigability: the number of peaks’, printed p. 2
overlaps.quote: 42% of the empirically derived landscapes (478 of 1,137) have multiple peaks of unequal height ... peak numbers ranging from 2 to 36
overlaps.definition_quote: a member of a plateau; For each TF, we calculated δ as the residual standard error; otherwise, we could not differentiate between the two affinity values.
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper treats neighboring affinities within a TF-specific noise threshold δ as unresolved plateau relationships. GraphFLA's required epsilon=0 baseline only treats exact ties as neutral; because no complete input was acquired, compatibility under the per-factor δ was not tested.

input.preprocessing: The paper points to UniPROBE and CIS-BP and gives the accession crosswalk in Supplementary Table 1. The full set of per-factor E-score data and the crosswalk were not reconstructed.

overlaps.graphfla_call: For each factor, DNALandscape().build_from_data(bound_sequences, e_scores, epsilon=TF_specific_delta, verbose=False), then aggregate the number of landscapes with n_lo > 1; not run.
overlaps.reason: The printed corpus target is an aggregate over the full set of transcription-factor landscapes. No complete per-factor input or accession mapping was acquired, so no GraphFLA aggregate was calculated.

overlaps.quote: sign epistasis is more frequent and affects 4.7% of squares, on average
overlaps.definition_quote: epistasis can be partitioned into ... magnitude, simple sign and reciprocal sign
overlaps.definition_divergence: The reported 4.7% is the average sign-epistasis fraction across landscapes, combining simple and reciprocal sign epistasis. A reproduction needs the same complete-square set, TF-specific δ decisions, and averaging across landscapes; these could not be checked without the source inputs.

input.preprocessing: Same unreconstructed UniPROBE/CIS-BP transcription-factor inputs as the n_lo target.

overlaps.graphfla_call: For each factor, graphfla.analysis.classify_epistasis(landscape).sign, then average per-factor values with the paper's weighting; not run.
overlaps.reason: The paper prints an aggregate class fraction, but the landscapes and TF-specific noise thresholds required to reproduce it were not acquired.

overlaps.paper_value: Per-landscape mean and standard deviation of the fraction of accessible paths; individual values are shown as plotted symbols.
overlaps.quote: For each of the 1,137 adaptive landscapes we show the mean (symbols) and standard deviation (error bars)
overlaps.definition_quote: fraction of accessible paths to the highest-affinity site in the landscape
overlaps.definition_divergence: The paper's per-landscape path fractions are plotted, not printed as a numeric summary. This GraphFLA metric was explicitly ruled out as a literature-validation target for this assignment.
overlaps.reason: No value was read from Figure 2c; the plotted points are not reproduction targets, and the user excluded global_optima_accessibility from literature validation.

paper_value.Gcn4: all 71 accessible mutational paths also increased gene expression monotonically
paper_value.Fhl1: all except one of the 37 accessible mutational paths increased gene expression monotonically

overlaps.locator: Results, ‘Gene expression reflects landscape topography’, printed p. 5
overlaps.quote: For Gcn4, all 71 accessible mutational paths ... for Fhl1 all except one of the 37 accessible mutational paths
overlaps.definition_quote: accessible mutational paths exhibit monotonic increases in gene expression
overlaps.definition_locator: Results, ‘Gene expression reflects landscape topography’, printed p. 5
overlaps.definition_divergence: These printed results ask whether gene expression is monotonic along already-accessible binding-affinity paths in a restricted in-vivo subset. They are not a fraction of accessible paths in each complete landscape or across the transcription-factor corpus.
overlaps.reason: The printed Gcn4/Fhl1 result concerns a second phenotype along selected paths and has no corresponding GraphFLA metric.

blockers.what: Supplementary Table 1 accession crosswalk and the full per-factor E-score inputs
blockers.why: The prior publisher request returned HTTP 200 with an HTML security challenge rather than an XLSX workbook. The failed body and checksum are preserved in papers/_core_lit_navigability/acquisition_codex.jsonl and referenced in the new acquisition log. The article identifies public UniPROBE/CIS-BP sources, but no complete per-factor input set was assembled.
blockers.needed_for: Reproducing the printed multi-peak aggregate, the sign-epistasis average, and any landscape-level peak-count range.

verdict_reason: The paper prints a strong aggregate n_lo overlap (478 of 1,137 landscapes have multiple peaks, with a printed range of 2–36) and a mean sign-epistasis fraction, but the complete inputs were not recovered. The individual peak-accessibility values are plotted; no mean, median, or single-peak landscape count is printed.
